title: Over a perfect field of characteristic different from 2 and 3, two elliptic curves have symplectically isomorphic Galois 3-torsion exactly when one is a smooth fiber of the other Weierstrass Hesse pencil
author: Ane S.I. Anema; Jaap Top; Anne Tuijp
source_version: Official SIGMA 14 (2018) article 102, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2018.102; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: A common geometric set of flex points is insufficient to classify elliptic curves with the same Galois torsion representation. The author combines explicit pencil discriminants with a count of all symplectic identifications and exceptional automorphism cases. Uniqueness of the projective map on four torsion points then supplies the essential Galois descent to the original perfect field.

source_check.note: The full original Theorem 1.1 is retained with its complete characteristic-not-2-or-3 branch, with the perfect-field and symplectic Galois-module requirements recorded on the cover. All flex/three-torsion/group-law/Weil-pairing identifications, explicit Weierstrass pencil and j/discriminant formulas, all 24 symplectic maps including exceptional j-values/infinity, four-point projective rigidity and the complete Hilbert-90 descent are bundled as new core/context. The source explicitly reports the polynomial discriminants as computer-algebra calculations; they are preserved as author formulas, without an independent rerun or reproof. The modified characteristic-two branch and anti-symplectic family are not added, and no neighboring support result is counted separately. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: Complete Sections2-8 proof of Theorem1.1 was read, selecting the characteristic different from2 and3 branch. The author proves flex/3-torsion identification and preservation of group law and Weil pairing along the pencil, gives explicit Weierstrass transformation and j/discriminant polynomials, and counts all24 symplectic torsion identifications including j=0,1728 and the infinity fiber. Four noncollinear torsion points uniquely determine the projective map, permitting Galois invariance and Hilbert90 descent. The Hessian identity and displayed polynomial discriminants are reported explicit computer-algebra calculations; no independent rerun or mathematical reproof is claimed. The separate modified characteristic2 construction is not selected.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem1.1 restricted to its complete Sections2-8 branch: k perfect with characteristic neither2 nor3, E and Eprime elliptic curves over k and E given by a Weierstrass equation. A Weil-pairing-preserving G_k-module isomorphism E[3] to Eprime[3] exists iff Eprime is k-isomorphic to a smooth fiber E_t0 of the Hessian pencil tF+Hess(F), with t0 in P^1(k), including infinity. The claim concerns symplectic Galois-module identifications, not arbitrary geometric torsion isomorphisms. The characteristic2 modified pencil and anti-symplectic family are not added.
